entries.title: FBI and Former US National Cyber Director Publicly Attribute Taiwan AI Infrastructure Attacks to Chinese Operators at Black Hat — New Development
entries.summary: Security officials at Black Hat publicly confirmed for the first time that suspected Chinese operators used open-source AI agents named Hermes and OpenClaw in near-autonomous attacks on Taiwanese government and energy sector targets, with FBI Cyber Division leadership and former US National Cyber Director Chris Inglis providing attribution — the first public US government naming of commodity open-source AI agents used against critical infrastructure.

links.title: AI Governance Institute: Open-Source AI Agents Used in Near-Autonomous Attacks on Taiwan Infrastructure

entries.title: Stripe Acquires AI Model Gateway OpenRouter for $7B+ — Payments Company Now Controls Multi-Model Routing Layer for 8 Million Developers
entries.summary: Stripe finalized a deal to acquire OpenRouter, which routes developer traffic across 400+ AI models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, and others, for more than $7 billion — a 5x markup from its $1.3B Series B valuation months earlier — placing payments infrastructure at the center of AI ecosystem access and raising AI concentration-of-power concerns.

links.title: Bloomberg: Stripe Finalizes Deal to Acquire OpenRouter for Over $7 Billion
TechCrunch: Stripe will reportedly acquire AI gateway startup OpenRouter for $7B+

entries.title: Stanford/Arc Institute Evo 2 Designs 16 Novel Functional Bacteriophages — Johns Hopkins Editorial in Science Warns Governance Gap Is Confirmed
entries.summary: Coverage and biosecurity governance analysis emerged this week around a study published August 6 in Science in which Stanford and Arc Institute researchers used the Evo 2 genomic language model to produce 16 working bacteriophage genomes matching no known natural sequence, with a companion editorial by Johns Hopkins biosecurity experts warning that existing DNA synthesis screening systems were not built to catch AI-generated novel sequences, exposing a critical dual-use governance gap.

links.title: AI Governance Institute: AI-Designed Viruses Expose a Dual-Use Gap in Enterprise Governance Programs
Stanford Report: AI designs a novel E. coli killer (Evo 2)

entries.title: arXiv 2608.13840 (ASSERT): Specification-Driven GenAI Audit Measurement Pipeline Shows Reported Behavioral Rates Move Substantially With Measurement Choices
entries.summary: Microsoft and collaborators introduce ASSERT, a pipeline that ties each GenAI audit's reported compliance rate to a written specification of measurement choices; a case study on conversational deception shows that the reported rate shifts significantly with dialogue setup, simulated user, judge selection, and evidence threshold, meaning different audits of the same system can produce incomparable numbers and even reversed model rankings.

links.title: arXiv 2608.13840: ASSERT: A Measurement Pipeline for GenAI Audits

entries.title: CISA and Cloud Security Alliance Publish Agentic AI Governance Standards: Cryptographic Agent Identity, Short-Lived Credentials, and Human-in-the-Loop for Irreversible Actions
entries.summary: CISA's agentic AI adoption guidance (analyzed this week by the Cloud Security Alliance) mandates cryptographically verified agent identities, short-lived credentials, encrypted agent-to-agent communications, least-privilege enforcement, and mandatory human-in-the-loop approval for irreversible or high-impact actions — setting binding federal security expectations for enterprise AI agent deployments, with a companion CSA document mapping these controls to NIST standards.

links.title: AI Governance Institute: CISA Agentic AI Guidance Sets Binding Identity and Approval Standards
AI Governance Institute: CSA Maps Agentic AI Controls to NIST Standards

entries.title: arXiv 2608.14399: Preregistered Algorithm Audit Finds LLMs Show Hidden Demographic Tilts in Physician Recommendations — Effects Never Appear in Models' Own Explanations
entries.summary: A randomized audit of 7 LLMs across 40,068 physician-choice scenarios finds statistically significant demographic tilts (female- and minority-signaled names gaining 1.3–2.9 pp over White-signaled names) that models never mention in their stated justifications, demonstrating that transparency obligations relying on model self-report would not detect these biases.

links.title: arXiv 2608.14399: Whose doctor does the AI recommend? An algorithm audit of LLM-assisted physician choice

entries.title: Training Data — Not Fine-Tuning, Scaling, or In-Context Learning — Sets Hard AI Capability Ceiling, Per MPI/ELLIS/ETH Zurich Study
entries.summary: Researchers from MPI for Intelligent Systems, ELLIS Institute Tübingen, and ETH Zurich trained language models on a corpus filtered to US elementary-school curriculum standards and found that scaling, fine-tuning, and in-context learning all fail to push performance meaningfully beyond what pretraining data contained — providing empirical grounding that training data scope is the primary determinant of model capability, with direct implications for capability prediction and pre-deployment evaluation.

links.title: AI Governance Institute: Training Data, Not Fine-Tuning, Sets the Hard Capability Ceiling for AI Models

entries.title: arXiv 2608.14329: LLM-as-Judge Loses 47 Accuracy Points Under Adversarial Keyword Stuffing in Principle-Based Financial Regulation — Benchmark Reveals 'Compliance Theatre'
entries.summary: A new four-axis benchmark (Principle-Bench) for LLM judges in FCA Consumer Duty and financial-promotion contexts finds that a 120B LLM-judge drops from 0.74 to 0.27 accuracy under keyword-stuffed inputs, two judges from different model families agree at only κ=0.16 on the worst split, and no method dominates all four axes of accuracy, paraphrase robustness, adversarial robustness, and calibration.

links.title: arXiv 2608.14329: A Four-Axis Trustworthiness Benchmark for LLM-as-Judge in Principle-Based Regulation

entries.title: arXiv 2608.13674: Conservative Reddit Political Discourse Homogenized Post-ChatGPT While Progressive Users Were Unaffected — Community-Level, Not Individual, Effect
entries.summary: A longitudinal study of 6 million Reddit comments (2019–2025) finds an asymmetric break in discourse diversification emerging around late 2022 in which conservative users experienced homogenization of political language while progressive users showed no comparable change, with stayer analysis localizing the effect to community-level discursive convergence rather than within-user AI adoption.

links.title: arXiv 2608.13674: Asymmetric Discourse Homogenization and Shared Language Technology: Evidence from Reddit

entries.title: arXiv 2608.14089 (Regime-Conditional Verification): Wrapper Adapts Off-the-Shelf Safety Classifiers to Deployer Policy Without Retraining — Catches 81% of Previously Missed Unsafe Content
entries.summary: RCV is a lightweight wrapper that estimates from a safety classifier's internal representations whether each prediction disagrees with the deployer's policy, selectively corrects likely-wrong predictions, and uses the same correctness estimates as a label-free distribution shift signal — improving policy adherence across all three tested classifiers and two benchmarks, and detecting every attack campaign in a deployment study.

links.title: arXiv 2608.14089: Regime-Conditional Verification: Correctness Estimation for Adapting and Monitoring Safety Classifiers

entries.title: CVE-2026-11624: NIST NVD Formalizes DNS Rebinding Risk in MCP Servers as Active Remediation Obligation
entries.summary: NIST's National Vulnerability Database recorded CVE-2026-11624 requiring Model Context Protocol servers to validate the Origin header on all incoming connections to prevent DNS rebinding attacks, treating origin validation as a mandatory hardening requirement for any enterprise running agent or tool servers built on MCP.

links.title: AI Governance Institute: CVE-2026-11624 — NIST Flags DNS Rebinding Risk in MCP Servers

entries.title: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol/Luna Update Creates Silent Model Change Management Obligations for Enterprise and Codex Deployments
entries.summary: OpenAI released updated GPT-5.6 family variants including new default models for free-tier users and an adjustable effort mode for paid tiers, with changes also affecting Codex and ChatGPT Work environments — meaning enterprise deployments may have received silent capability changes that existing approvals, access controls, and audit configurations may not cover.

links.title: AI Governance Institute: OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Update Triggers Model Change Management Obligations

entries.title: MCP Project Publishes First Official Sandboxing Baseline for Enterprise Agent Deployments — Sets Measurable Gap for Existing Deployments
entries.summary: The Model Context Protocol project published formal security best practices requiring sandboxing or containerization for spawned processes and restricting file system access for MCP servers, giving compliance teams an official measurable standard against which to evaluate existing deployments that lack these controls.

links.title: AI Governance Institute: MCP Project Publishes Sandboxing Baseline for Enterprise Agent Deployments
